title: Key management & regulatory boundaries discovery - Ironclad Bancorp
summary: Intro + constraints on key residency and logs, tradeoff discussion hosted vs dedicated vs private, ask for SOC2/HIPAA artifacts, propose pilot for KMS integration and log redaction proof-of-concept.
topics: Log collection, redaction and retention windows
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
questions: Can Redwood guarantee keys never leave EU region?
What logs are captured by default and can we redact PII before they leave our VPC?
What SLAs exist for Dedicated and Private?
next_steps: Samir to send SOC2, HIPAA and private deployment architecture docs by 2027-05-24
Lena to schedule a technical runbook session and KMS integration workshop week of 2027-05-31
Customer to confirm pilot dataset and success metrics by 2027-05-26
action_items: Samir Patel: Email SOC2 + HIPAA package and link to controls spreadsheet (due 2027-05-24)
Lena Ortiz: Prep KMS/HSM integration doc and sample Terraform snippets (due 2027-05-28)

transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-05-19 16:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Attendees: Samir, Lena (Redwood) / Maya, Oliver, Priya (Ironclad)

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. I'm Samir, AE at Redwood Inference. With me is Lena our SE. How are you all?
[00:07] Maya Chen: Doing well, thanks. We'll keep this focused, Priya will flag anything legal.
[00:12] Oliver Grant: Morning from my side. We've got a pretty tight compliance matrix with regional key residency and log rules.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Great, understand. High level, today we'd love to map your constraints and go over hosting options — hosted, dedicated, private — and how keys and logs behave in each.
[00:27] Priya Nair: Specifically: can we prevent private keys from leaving the EU, do you have HSM integrations, and what logs are captured end-to-end?
[00:34] Lena Ortiz: Yep, we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For Private deployments keys can be customer-controlled and never leave the customer's VPC. For Hosted, we offer envelope encryption but keys are managed by Redwood unless you opt for a dedicated KMS path.
[00:46] Maya Chen: Can you clarify "dedicated KMS path"? We need proof that keys are resident in our Azure subscription.
[00:52] Lena Ortiz: Right, so "dedicated KMS path" means we can set up an integration where calls to decrypt go to your KMS via a private peering. In practice that means the root of trust stays in your tenancy. For our Hosted public API we have a multi-tenant KMS model unless we set up a dedicated connection as part of an enterprise contract.
[01:05] Oliver Grant: That sounds promising. But the next question is logs. We have strict retention windows for transaction metadata and must strip PII before logs leave our environment. What are your redaction options?
[01:16] Samir Patel: Default telemetry captures request metadata, errors, latencies, token counts; we don't store raw customer prompts by default in Dedicated/Private. In Hosted, we do store request bodies for troubleshooting unless opted out. But we can enable automatic masking, prefix caching suppressed, and configurable log streams.
[01:30] Priya Nair: "We do store" is too vague. Our compliance team requires audit trails that show whether data was redacted and the hash of original inputs. Can Redwood provide cryptographic fingerprints without retaining plaintext?
[01:42] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we have a mode to compute SHA256 hashes of inputs client-side — we store the hash and some client-provided metadata, but not the raw prompt. For Private deployments that's trivial. Hosted requires an enterprise connector. There's also the option to run an inline redaction lambda that strips PII before any telemetry leaves your VPC.
[01:58] Maya Chen: Inline lambda — is that something you provide or we build?
[02:02] Lena Ortiz: We can provide reference code and a managed option in Dedicated where we operate the redaction in your VPC via a cross-account role.
[02:11] Oliver Grant: Ok, so if we choose Dedicated with a VNet peering and our KMS, keys never leave our tenancy and logs can be pre-redacted. What about fallback behavior? If the Dedicated pool is saturated do requests flip to hosted models and leak things to Redwood-managed infra?
[02:27] Samir Patel: Good question. We have routing policies. For strict compliance we can configure automatic failover to other Dedicated pools only, not to Hosted. If you want full isolation we can disable cross-fallback and set hard capacity alerts. 
[02:41] Priya Nair: We also need SOC2 and HIPAA artifacts as part of our vendor review. Can you provide attestation and specific control mappings?
[02:49] Samir Patel: Absolutely. I'll send our SOC2 Type II report, the HIPAA self-attestation, and a control matrix mapping Redwood controls to common frameworks.
[02:56] Maya Chen: Please also include the private deployment architecture diagram and network path for KMS calls.
[03:01] Samir Patel: Yep, will include. I'll put the diagram and a sample runbook.
[03:05] [03:05] Lena Ortiz: A couple technical notes — KV cache terms: when doing chat with long contexts the KV/cache can leak prefix tokens unless you pin the session to Private mode. For privacy sensitive contexts we recommend disabling shared cache and enabling session pinning.
[03:22] Oliver Grant: There was a recent paper on cache leaks — so we'll need to ensure no shared cache across tenants.
[03:27] Lena Ortiz: Agreed. Dedicated and Private have tenant isolation on caches. Hosted has an option to opt-out of shared prefix caching.
[03:35] Maya Chen: Let's talk about region locking. Our EU customers' data must stay in EU for processing and storage. Is that doable with Hosted?
[03:42] Samir Patel: Hosted has regional endpoints — EU region is supported, but for stricter guarantees we recommend Dedicated in the customer region or Private. Hosted can route to EU-only compute but certain control plane metadata may be in Redwood control plane in US unless you opt for a private control plane.
[03:58] Priya Nair: Private control plane — what does that entail? Is it a separate control plane we host in our environment?
[04:04] Lena Ortiz: For Private deployments we deploy a customer-specific control plane that you manage or we manage in your VPC. That keeps metadata and audit logs local. It's slightly heavier in ops but meets the strictest residency requirements.
[04:15] Oliver Grant: Ops burden is a concern. We prefer minimal engineering toil. How much work for onboarding Private?
[04:20] Lena Ortiz: Typical Private onboarding is 4–8 weeks depending on approvals and network setup. Dedicated is faster, usually 2–4 weeks. Hosted is immediate for proofs of concept.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Cost is another factor. Can you provide estimates for per-token cost on Dedicated vs Hosted and any uplift for KMS peering or private control plane?
[04:40] Samir Patel: We'll put together a cost sheet. Roughly Dedicated has a baseline reserved capacity price plus lower per-token consumption. Private includes a platform fee and potentially egress/peering charges. I'll include ranges in the follow-up.
[04:52] [04:52] Oliver Grant: On encryption, we need HSM-backed keys for certain flows. Does Redwood support custom HSM integrations or only cloud KMS?
[04:59] Lena Ortiz: We support cloud KMS providers (Azure Key Vault, AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and partner HSMs via PKCS#11 in Private. For Dedicated we can integrate through a customer HSM gateway. It's a typical enterprise configuration.
[05:12] Priya Nair: We also have to show separation of duties and admin access. Who has access to logs and keys at Redwood?
[05:19] Samir Patel: In Dedicated/Private, admin access can be scoped to customer SSO identities. For Hosted we have RBAC internally and SAML for customer admins. We can provide the list of Redwood roles with descriptions in the controls package.
[05:30] Maya Chen: Audit retention — we need immutable retention for 7 years for specific transaction logs. Is that supported?
[05:36] Lena Ortiz: We can keep immutable WORM-style retention if you manage the storage in your tenancy (Private). Hosted has retention up to X days by default but enterprise retention can be negotiated — however immutability is easiest when customer controls storage.
[05:50] Oliver Grant: For the pilot, we want to validate that redaction works and keys are never exposed. Proposed flow: Dedicated in EU, KMS in our Azure tenancy, inline redaction lambda, run 100k queries with synthetic PII and verify hashes and no plaintext stored. Does that sound doable?
[06:07] Samir Patel: Totally doable. We'll scope the pilot and include runbook, test dataset template, and success criteria like zero plaintext logged, KMS call logs showing no outbound key copies, and latency targets.
[06:18] Priya Nair: Who will run the initial bench? Your SE or our cloud team?
[06:22] Lena Ortiz: We typically pair — Redwood SE runs a templated benchmark while your cloud team monitors the KMS side. We'll make sure telemetry is mutually agreeable.
[06:31] [06:31] Maya Chen: A few quick nitpicks — we need to see evidence of SSO integration working with our Okta, and proof that support staff cannot escalate to view plaintext.
[06:39] Samir Patel: We'll include Okta SAML docs and an admin access policy. We can also show logs of role-based access in our Dedicated tenants.
[06:46] Oliver Grant: What about legal hold — if regulators request certain records, how do we deliver without violating residency constraints?
[06:52] Lena Ortiz: For Private, all data is in your environment so you can export. For Dedicated we can provide export with controls to filter by region and custodian. For Hosted it depends on where the data is stored. We have processes to support legal hold but some steps require cross-team approvals.
[07:06] Priya Nair: Ok. For our procurement team we need pricing, SOC2 + HIPAA docs, network diagrams, and a proposed pilot plan in next week's window.
[07:14] Samir Patel: We'll deliver that. Lena, any technical appendices you want to call out?
[07:19] Lena Ortiz: A couple: sample Terraform for KMS peering, example redaction lambda in Python, and a sample telemetry schema that shows which fields we capture. I'll include those in the repo link.
[07:31] Maya Chen: Good. Also, can you confirm geo-fencing for model weights? We can't have weights replicated outside EU for certain models.
[07:39] Samir Patel: Model weights can be region-locked for Private and Dedicated; Hosted may replicate weights to multiple regions for availability unless we do a dedicated regional deployment. We'll note that in the follow-up.
[07:52] Oliver Grant: Any limitations on model variants when running Private? For example, large decoder models — do you support the same quantizations?
[07:59] Lena Ortiz: We support the open model catalog and most quantization profiles. Some bleeding-edge kernels may require specific drivers; we'll capture compatibility matrix for your target GPUs.
[08:09] [08:09] Priya Nair: Thanks. From legal perspective: we need indemnities and subcontractor lists. Is Redwood willing to sign a data processing agreement with EU addendum?
[08:18] Samir Patel: Yes, we have a standard DPA with EU Addendum. We'll circulate it.
[08:22] Maya Chen: Great. Let's capture next steps then.
[08:26] Samir Patel: Recap — I'll send SOC2/HIPAA, architecture diagrams, cost ranges, and proposed pilot runbook by 2027-05-24. Lena will attach KMS integration notes and Terraform. Customer to provide pilot dataset specs and regulatory carve-outs by 2027-05-26. We'll reconvene week of 2027-05-31 for an SE-led workshop.
[08:44] Oliver Grant: Sounds good. One last quick concern — if we do Dedicated, do you offer runbook handover and a 30/90 day hypercare?
[08:51] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Dedicated includes onboarding support and we can contract a hypercare period in the pilot SOW.
[08:58] Priya Nair: Ok thanks everyone.
[09:00] Samir Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up.
